name: text-to-cad
one_liner: Lets an AI assistant design, check, and prepare real physical parts — 3D models, engineering drawings, robot parts, 3D-print files — from a plain description, instead of needing a trained CAD engineer at the keyboard.
buyer: A hardware startup founder or product designer who can't afford a full-time mechanical engineer but needs to iterate on part designs fast.
business_use_cases: A small hardware startup uses it to generate and dimension a custom enclosure, skipping a $5k-a-month contract CAD engineer for early iterations.
A maker running a 3D-printing side business uses it to turn customer sketches into printable, pre-checked STL files same-day.
A robotics hobbyist studio uses the URDF/SDF skills to spin up simulator-ready robot models for client demos without a robotics specialist.

money_ideas.idea: Run a 'describe it, get a printable part' service for makers and small inventors: they send a sketch or sentence, you deliver a checked STEP/STL file.
Offer a subscription CAD-ops add-on for hardware startups: ongoing part iteration, DFM review, and vendor (SendCutSend) handoff.

steal_this: This weekend, build a simple intake form where someone describes a bracket or enclosure in plain English and gets back a dimensioned PDF drawing plus an STL, priced per part.
